qualitative.text: LUCI sounding rocket, PMMA rod, simulated lunar gravity: chamber O2 fell from 20% to 14.3% and the flame died after about 6 cm. Not a controlled-O2 limit.
LUCI ground reference, same rod, 1 g: chamber O2 fell from 21% to 14.5% during the burn.
LUCI, SIBAL fabric, simulated lunar gravity, downward in air: steady spread, flame base 0.92 mm/s.
Ferkul 2026, SIBAL fabric, aircraft at 0.165 g, 21% O2: steady downward spread for the full 20 s test, 0.086 cm/s.
Ferkul 2026, SIBAL fabric, centrifuge drop rig, air at 1 atm: downward spread at 0.11 cm/s.
Zayac 2024, SIBAL fabric burns downward in lunar-gravity air but goes out right after ignition in 1 g. No O2 value is given.
Urban 2025, PMMA, tape and cotton T-shirt at 8.2 psia in lunar gravity: a lower O2 limit than extrapolated from 1 g. Values are plot only.
Urban 2025, polycarbonate and Nomex Velcro at 8.2 psia in lunar gravity: needed higher O2 than the 1 g data predict. Values are plot only.
Sacksteder 2003, thin cellulose tissue on aircraft flights at 0.1, 0.16 and 0.38 g in 21% O2: upward spread varied linearly with gravity. Reduced-pressure air, not a spacecraft material.

summary.headline: No measured test reaches 34% O2 at 8.2 psia in lunar gravity.
summary.headline_detail: Highest lunar-gravity O2 figure in these sources: about 29% (Nomex HT90-40 fabric, 8.2 psi, preliminary).
